summary.headline: Tech Mahindra Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.8% YoY to US$1,693M and EBIT margin hit 14.8%, with US$1,023M deal wins.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ and 7.2% YoY in constant currency, with organic growth of 7% YoY in CC, led by Communications ramp-up on the Orange large deal. EBIT margin of 14.8% expanded 40 bps QoQ and 260 bps YoY, and management reiterated a full-year FY27 EBIT margin target of 15%. Free cash flow was US$135M, held back by rebadged-deal ramp-ups that management expects to normalise next quarter. Management emphasised AI (Helix, Zero-Gravity Telco Architecture) and a shift in the three-year plan toward growth, with the next plan to be announced later.

financial_highlights.change: US$ PAT +23.2% YoY; PAT margin +130 bps YoY
Impacted by rebadged deal ramp-up; FCF-to-PAT guidance 90-100% reiterated
MTM movement US$13.83M: US$8.7M in P&L, US$5M in reserves

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9.5% YoY and 6% QoQ, driven by Orange large-deal ramp-up and new strategic engagements; management says pipeline and visibility remain strong despite client concentration.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 4.6% YoY (5.4% CC) and 0.4% QoQ (1% QoQ CC); management said prior two quarters were above 8% and expects a return to that level next quarter, with leadership changes made.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY but declined 3.9% QoQ after accelerated execution of a large European automotive program in Q1; a further sequential headwind of about 0.5% is expected in Q3.

segments.name: Retail, Travel and Logistics
segments.commentary: Grew 9.2% YoY (about 9.5-9.6% per call) and 9.6% QoQ, supported by new deal scale-up and growth in existing accounts; fastest-growing vertical per management.

segments.name: Hi-Tech / TME / Healthcare
segments.commentary: Hi-Tech grew 6.7% YoY; Technology, Media and Entertainment grew 2.8% QoQ; Healthcare grew 6.2% YoY and 1.4% QoQ.

segments.name: Service lines
segments.commentary: Digital enterprise applications (ServiceNow, Salesforce, SAP, Oracle) grew about 13% YoY; ADMS grew 7.6% YoY; BPS grew 6.5% YoY; experience design and consulting were relatively weaker.

segments.name: Large accounts (>US$20M)
segments.commentary: Revenue from accounts above US$20M grew 3.1% QoQ and 11.7% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% reiterated; management said the company is on track and within about 20 bps of its margin aspiration.
Free cash flow to PAT of 90-100% on a full-year basis reiterated.
Capital allocation policy of returning 85% and above of free cash flow to shareholders reaffirmed.
Q3 FY27 sequential headwind from European auto program expected at roughly 0.5%, to normalise thereafter.
Management expects normal seasonality in H2 FY27 with no unusual furloughs in Q3 or Q4.
AI revenue reporting to be introduced as part of H2 FY27 disclosures.
Next three-year plan to be announced later; management signalled growth will be the focus and no specific growth number was given.
capex_capacity: Board recommended a 1:1 bonus share issue; interim dividend of INR15 per share declared.
Launched Toronto Innovation Hub and Engineering Experience Center, building on Manufacturing, Communication and Retail CPG Experience Centers.
Launched Consumer Agentic Experience Studio (more than 20 customers hosted since launch) and Indus-Terra, a 30-billion-parameter model built with NVIDIA and AWS under IndiaAI Mission.
AI Velocity Cells program delivered 16 client-relevant capstones in seven weeks; portfolio includes more than 200 AI assets being rationalised.
IHub Quantum partnership: middleware for India's 20-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer, completion expected by December 2026.
demand_pricing: Deal wins of US$1,023M in the quarter were broad-based across Comms, BFSI, Manufacturing and Retail/Logistics/Transport; wins include a Canadian insurer (ApMS), a UK digital network mainframe-as-a-service deal, and a 5-year Australian telecom managed services deal.
Management said pricing pressure is driven more by competitive intensity than by budget diversion to AI; AI token costs are not a material part of client IT budgets.
Outcome-based and human-plus-agent pricing (including Vector Squad-based pricing for F&A) is gaining adoption across telco and financial services.
Management argued that AI model commoditisation resembles cloud, with clients using multiple models including open-source, which it sees as supporting services demand.
Management expects some productivity release from fixed-price contracts via AI toolchains, but sees growth opportunity in consulting, modernization, data and analytics.

qa_highlights.question: How are service-line offerings like TechM Orion driving share gains and where is momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital enterprise applications grew about 13% YoY and BPS 6.5% YoY; management sees AI toolchains per service line plus industry roadmaps driving above-industry growth. Consulting and experience design were relatively weaker.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin expansion nearing its peak given headcount increased this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the headcount rise to the Orange deal employee transfer and said gross margin opportunity is not fully tapped; AI toolchains should release headcount from fixed-price projects, and Rohit said gross margin gains will continue for the next three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company trade margin for growth, aiming for near double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said the focus will pivot to profitable growth in year three of the roadmap and will not buy revenue; he declined to give a number for the next three-year plan.

qa_highlights.question: Can Communications and BFSI drive medium-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Comms pipeline is strong but concentrated; BFSI grew 5.4% CC, was above 8% in the prior two quarters, and management expects a return to that level next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are growth gains coming from large accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Accounts above US$20M grew 11.7% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, and management said these accounts still have significant headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI capex slowdown shift enterprise budgets toward services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI token spend is small for clients; hardware and cloud cost increases from the AI build-out could ease, freeing budget for services, but it is hard to quantify benefit given competitive pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the European auto revenue impact a reversal and how big is the Q3 effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit clarified it is a ramp-up from Q1 leading to QoQ declines in Q2 and Q3, not a reversal; Q3 impact is about 0.5% and then normalises.

risks_watch: Free cash flow was US$135M, held back by rebadged-deal ramp-up; management expects normalisation next quarter, and DSO rose four days QoQ to 88 days.
Effective tax rate of 29.9% included a one-time prior-period adjustment; underlying rate was 26.6%.
AI-driven deflation in effort-based fixed-price and managed services contracts could pressure revenue, and management acknowledged ADMS renewals carry productivity expectations that may mute growth.
Comms revenue is highly concentrated among a few clients, adding volatility.
European automotive weakness in Manufacturing, with a further sequential headwind in Q3.
AI revenue disclosure methodology is still being defined and will start in H2 FY27.
Growth in BFSI remains below the company's aspiration; leadership changes made.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and AI, with management repeatedly stating the quarter was strong and the margin target near. Cautious on specifics: declined to give a next three-year growth number, and was defensive on BFSI underperformance and on AI deflation questions.
key_quotes: We delivered a very strong quarter with broad -based growth across the business.
We do expect, as a result of the specific AI toolchain, we're building for each and every single service line, to be able to release head count across our fixed-price projects
We don't believe for a moment that the gross margin opportunities in the business have been fully tapped out
Our principle is simple. AI revenue must be evidenced by client -funded work and reconcilable to financial records.

growth.why: Reported revenue up 6.8% YoY (7.2% CC, 7% organic) with US$1,023M quarterly deal wins and LTM deal wins up 34.8%, and FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% reiterated; no revenue growth number was guided and no new capacity is being added, so backing is partial (order book and Orange ramp-up) rather than capacity-based.

mgmt.note: Management referenced leadership changes made in BFSI but gave no named new top-management stance or growth plan for them on this call.
